title: Metric cartography - latency, uptime, econ signals canvas
content:
Purpose: quick, QBR-ready reference that maps our primary operational signals (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate) to measurement rules, visualizations to include in an executive QBR slide, and a short playbook for renewal conversations. This is intentionally compact and slightly opinionated — use it as the canonical 'how we package signals for customers' draft.

Notes to self / context:
- Audience: CSM + Solutions + AE for pre-QBR prep; also useful for internal SRE handoff when a customer flags performance/regression.
- Tone: prescriptive but light — include formulas and simple examples so non-technical execs can read the KPI table.
- Data sources: Redwood Console traces (latency percentiles), billing export (cost/token), CDN/cache metrics + runtime KV cache logs (cache-hit), platform health events + synthetic checks (uptime).

Metric definitions and measurement rules:
1) Latency (token/response latency)
   - Core idea: measure user-visible response speed for generation requests.
   - Primary SLI: p95 downstream-response-time (end-to-end from API ingress to first-byte returned) measured in ms.
   - Window: rolling 7-day and 30-day windows for QBR snapshot.
   - Formula: p95 = 95th percentile of sample of all completed generation requests where status = 200 and model_version = customer_pinned_version.
   - Include: both full-response latency and first-byte latency (for streaming customers) — label columns p95_full_ms and p95_firstbyte_ms.
   - Example: 7-day p95_full = 340 ms. How we present: show trend sparkline (30d), current 7d p95, delta vs prior 30d, and % of requests above SLA threshold.

2) Uptime (availability)
   - Core idea: fraction of successful API responses (status 200/2xx) out of total requests, plus synthetic probe pass-rate for route-level availability.
   - Primary SLI: availability_pct = (successful_requests / total_requests) * 100 measured daily and aggregated to 30d.
   - Window: daily, with 30-day aggregate shown in QBR.
   - Measurement rules: exclude maintenance windows that were pre-announced (tagged in maintenance log). Exclude user errors (4xx) from denominator when computing platform availability for platform-SLA discussions; for customer-facing experience include 4xx as a separate column.
   - Example: 30d availability_pct = 99.92%.

3) Cost per token (econ)
   - Core idea: unit economics of serving — how much the customer is spending per generated token in the last billing period. Useful for renewal conversations about optimizing model variant / quantization / batching.
   - Primary SLI: cost_per_1k_tokens = (total_billing_amount_usd / total_generated_tokens) * 1000.
   - Data sources: billing export (line items) matched to request logs by date/model/route where possible; if not matchable at token-level, use model-level estimated tokens from logs + prorated billing.
   - Window: last invoice period (monthly) with a 3-month rolling trend.
   - Example calc: total_billing = $12,400, tokens = 98,432,000 -> cost_per_1k_tokens = (12400 / 98,432,000) * 1000 = $0.126 per 1k tokens.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix / KV caching)
   - Core idea: fraction of requests that got partial/full answer from cache (prefix, KV cache, or inference-level memoization) vs those that required fresh full-decoding. Higher hit = lower cost and often lower latency.
   - Primary SLI: cache_hit_pct = (cache_hits / cache_lookups) * 100. For prefix caches include partial_hit_pct for partial-prefix matches.
   - Window: 7d rolling and 30d. Break down by route and by model variant.
   - Measurement guidance: ensure that cache lookups counted include only cacheable requests — exclude streaming-only routes where caching logic differs.
   - Example: 7d cache_hit_pct = 24%; partial_hit_pct = 8%. Present both as stacked bars in QBR.

KPI snapshot template (text table for QBR slide)
Columns: Metric | Primary SLI (unit) | Snapshot (value) | 30d trend | Threshold / SLA | Action tier (CS/SRE/Platform)
Rows (sample):
- Latency p95_full_ms | ms | 340 | ↑7% (30d) | SLA: p95 < 500 ms | CS: note to customer; SRE: examine slow tail; infra: consider model variant fallback
- Latency p99_ms | ms | 980 | ↑12% | SLA: p99 < 1500 ms | SRE + infra deep dive
- Availability_pct | % | 99.92 | -0.03% | SLA: 99.9% | CS flagged if <99.9; SRE if incident window exists
- Cost_per_1k_tokens | $ | 0.126 | ↓4% | Budget threshold: $0.15 | CS discuss optimizations; Solutions propose quantized model
- Cache_hit_pct | % | 24 | +2% | No hard SLA; target >30% for high-volume templates | Solutions: encourage prefix templating; Eng: tweak cache TTLs

Visualization recommendations for QBR slide:
- Top-left: single-line executive tile with three phrases: "Latency: p95 340ms (7d) | Availability 99.92% | Cost/1k $0.126"
- Middle: 30d stacked chart showing latency percentile bands (p50/p95/p99), colored by SLA exceedances.
- Right: small econ panel — bar chart with cost per 1k tokens across last 3 months + annotation for model variants causing spikes.
- Bottom: heatmap by route of cache_hit_pct (routes on y-axis), with churn signals overlaid (requests per route).

Playbook snippets: when to escalate / renewal messaging lines
- Small drift (latency p95 up <20% from baseline, availability still ≥ SLA): "Observed tail latency drift that may be addressed via batching and cache tuning; recommend pilot of prefix templates to recover ~10–20% cost and ~15–25% tail latency."
- Moderate regression (p95 up 20–60% or cost per 1k increased >25%): schedule technical deep-dive, propose Dedicated burst capacity trial or model-variant A/B to validate improvement. For renewal: frame as opportunity to reduce TCO by X% with a short pilot.
- Severe incident (availability < SLA or p99 > 2x baseline): immediate incident process (SRE page), require post-incident review, and neutral renewal risk flagged to AE.

Data quality / caveats / open questions (put these on the QBR prep checklist):
- Ensure model_version filter applied consistently — mixed-version requests will skew p99.
- Billing-to-log matching: some customers use multiple payment projects; confirm mapping in advance.
- Caching semantics vary by customer — ask solutions if they implement client-side dedupe.
- For streaming-heavy customers, use first-byte latency in SLAs rather than full-response.

QBR prep checklist (CSM actions):
- [ ] Run 30d and 7d reports for the metrics above at least 5 business days before QBR.
- [ ] Confirm maintenance windows and exclude them from availability calculation (link maintenance ID).
- [ ] Get model-version pin details from customer (ensure SLI filters aligned).
- [ ] Prepare 1–2 action recommendations: a quick optimization (cache TTL change / templating), and a medium one (model variant or Dedicated trial) with estimated cost savings.
- [ ] Add short narrative bullet: what changed since last QBR and why it matters for renewal.

Appendix: short formulas and sample code pointers
- p95 calc: use sample distribution from console.trace.latency_ms and compute 95th percentile; prefer approximate streaming algorithm for large samples.
- cost per 1k: (SUM(billing.usage_amount_usd) / SUM(requests.tokens_generated)) * 1000. Use monthly invoice as fallback.
- cache hit rate: (SUM(cache_hits) / SUM(cache_lookups)) * 100. For partial hits compute byte-equivalent saved if available.

Unresolved / backlog items to make this doc more canonical:
- Agree on single canonical 'first-byte' vs 'full-response' naming for publishing in one-pager.
- Standardize a single mapping table between billing line items and model tags (for easier cost calculations).
- Add a small Tableau template (or CSV-export format) for automated QBR slide generation.

End notes (tone for CS exec slide): keep it short: one-line summary (health: green/yellow/red), 3 metrics with arrows (latency, availability, cost), 1 recommended action. Use detailed appendix if exec asks for more.

—— scratch notes / ideas to consider later:
- Add a renewal-risk heuristic score computed as weighted sum of normalized metric deltas (weights: availability 0.4, latency 0.25, cost 0.2, cache 0.15).
- Pilot an automated QBR email that surfaces the top 2 technical recommendations + an expected delta in monthly spend if accepted.
